basics.name: Matias Barandiaran
basics.label: Computer Scientist
basics.summary: A Computer Science graduate from Lancaster University with over a year of research experience and a strong interest in software development, machine learning, and data engineering.

work.name: Technical University of Munich
work.summary: Hosted by the Gagneur Lab in affiliation with Helmholtz Munich.
highlights: Worked on rare variant association testing using deep learning and data-driven burden scores (DeepRVAT), utilizing Python, R, PyTorch and Snakemake
First-hand exposure to HPC cluster management, Linux, and Git version control

work.name: Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg
work.summary: Hosted by the Faculty of Medicine.
highlights: Worked on novel graph-level anomaly detection via latent space searching and generative adversarial networks (gladGAN) on molecular datasets, utilizing Python and PyTorch, and scikit-learn.

work.name: Lancaster University Leipzig
work.summary: Laboratory assistant and demonstrator for the Digital Systems module.
highlights: Delivered engaging and informative instructional sessions to facilitate student understanding on low-level programming with MIPS assembly.

work.name: Charles University
work.summary: Hosted by the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics.
highlights: Designed production of Alethe verifiable proofs for the GOLEM Constrained Horn Clauses solver, utilizing C++.
Contributed to the paper: Unsatisfiability Proofs for Horn Solving (2025) *won ETAPS best paper award*.
First-hand exposure to Linux, the software development life cycle, continuous integration, object-oriented programming, and software verification.

volunteer.summary: Co-Initiated and championed the approval process of Lancaster University’s Global Advancement Fund (≈€20k) to facilitate international collaboration between campuses worldwide
highlights: Took 7 members of the Leipzig campus to the UK for a 4-day trip to work on an industrial waste sorting arm.

volunteer.summary: Organized and hosted a Quantum Computing (QC) event powered by IBM.
highlights: Gave an introductory talk on QC and held workshops with Qiskit material.
Assembled a series of seminars with special guests like Enrique Solano (Co-CEO of Kipu Quantum).

volunteer.summary: Founded the computer science society at my institution.
highlights: Dedicated to fostering a culture of innovation, diversity and problem-solving with a focus on robotics.
Secured university funding for the purchase of robotics supplies (e.g. 3D printer, Arduinos, etc.).

courses: University ranked #132 worldwide for Computer Science (QS by subject) in 2025.
